RFC5798-5.1.1.3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 5.1.1.3 says "The TTL MUST be set to 255." TestSendAdvertV3IPv4HeaderTTLProtoDst changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same; it still requires frame[8] == 255. Single-polarity per the row annotation. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-5.1.1.3-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 5.1.1.3 says "A VRRP router receiving a packet with the TTL not equal to 255 MUST discard the packet." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. N4 with TTL 64 still requires ErrTTL. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-5.1.2.3-1.note: single-polarity by annotation: integration test reads IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS 255 back from the tx socket; runs only under the privileged QEMU suite

RFC5798-5.1.2.3-2.note: golden v6 decode passes at hop limit 255; hop limit 64 asserts ErrTTL

RFC5798-5.2.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 5.2.2 says "The only packet type defined in this version of the protocol is: 1 ADVERTISEMENT A packet with unknown type MUST be discarded." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. Type 2 still requires ErrType before the VRID lookup. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-5.2.4-1.note: owner EffectivePriority(0)==255 from configured 120; non-owner keeps 100

RFC5798-5.2.4-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): config range: TestBoundaryPriority accepts 1 and 254 and refuses 0 and 255; run-time: TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking (now tagged here) requires exact values including the floor at 1 for decrements equal to and past the priority (254/254, 100/100, 100/4064), so removing the clamp goes red. Record: revert EffectivePriority.

RFC5798-5.2.6-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 5.2.6 says "This field MUST be set to zero on transmission and ignored on reception." TestEncodeGoldenV3IPv4 now runs a subtest per checksum mode, and each still requires the rsvd nibble to be zero and the exact golden bytes; TestEncodeV3ReserveZeroOverDirtyBuffer encodes over an all-0xFF buffer against the default-mode golden G2. The reception half is TestDecodeV3ReserveIgnoredOnReceive, unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-5.2.8-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 5.2.8 says "The checksum is the 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum of the entire VRRP message starting with the version field and a "pseudo-header" as defined in Section 8.1 of [RFC2460]. The next header field in the ..." Ze now computes this form for IPv4 only in a group configured checksum rfc5798-compatible, because RFC 9568 Section 5.2.8, which obsoletes this text, says the IPv4 checksum "only includes the VRRP message"; the default IPv4 group neither sends nor accepts it, and the earlier sentence about dual-accept is withdrawn. TestFillChecksumFamilies (v3v4 under rfc5798-compatible) and TestFillChecksumZeroesFieldAndCoversPseudoHeader pin the IPv4 pseudo-header sum 0xDEFB and the IPv6 one in every mode; an overlay mutant forcing verifyReceived to the message-only form reddened the compatible-mode decodes. The only proof that a compatible group carries the mode from instance.doSendAdvert to the wire is the keepalived interop scenario, which no tag names. Enforced for the compatible mode only.

RFC5798-5.2.9-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 5.2.9 says "For IPv6, the first address must be the IPv6 link-local address associated with the virtual router." TestSendAdvertIPv6LeadsWithLinkLocal changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same; octets 8-24 are still required to be fe80::1 ahead of 2001:db8::1. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-5.2.9-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestValidateVIPFamilyMatchesGroupFamily now isolates both mixed-family cases: the IPv4 group lists 192.0.2.1 then 2001:db8::1, the IPv6 group lists fe80::1 then 192.0.2.1 (so the first-address-link-local rule cannot refuse it), and each refusal must carry the family error text; same-family lists validate. Records: revert validateGroup, both polarities.

RFC5798-6.1-1.note: ICMPv6 135 and 136 accepts must precede the first drop of the accept-filter chain; the test fails if either is missing or placed after a drop

RFC5798-6.4.2-3.note: Backup emits zero announcements; the Master's one announcement is BuildNA type 136, never 134

RFC5798-6.4.2-4.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuation 3): Wiring now proven on the host: TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState drives the FSM and asserts the worker sets the discard on the virtual router MAC device at start (idle worker: on then off), entering Backup adds no call, promotion withdraws it once after the only install, and a higher-priority advert demotes and sets it again before the only removal (records observed red on doRemoveVIPs; the run revert was also observed red but the ledger keeps one record per unit/polarity). Wire effect: TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest) forwards a transit datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC without the nft drop and stops it with it (records on backupFilterTables). RFC5798-6.4.2-5.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: Backup installs no VIP so no packet to it is delivered locally; Master contrast installs it

RFC5798-6.4.2-7.note: vrrp final judge 2026-09-29 (independent): earlier proof stands (promotion action list, StartAdvertTimer at the own interval, GARP per IPv4 VIP with the virtual router MAC, NA per IPv6 VIP R=1 S=0 O=1 TLL 00-00-5e-00-02-0a, stale-generation negative). The Solicited-Node clause is now asserted at Ze's boundary: TestPromotionInstallsIPv6AddressesOnVirtualMACDevice requires nothing installed in Backup and, on the Master_Down_Timer, exactly fe80::1 and 2001:db8::1 installed on the virtual-MAC device, never the parent -- the address add from which Linux addrconf joins each Solicited-Node group (record: doInstallVIPs). Wire effect: TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest) forwards the datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC once the filter is withdrawn and the address installed, and not while the filter holds (records on clearBackupFilter).

RFC5798-7.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify that the VRRP version is 3." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. N9 still requires ErrVersion for a v2 advert at a v3 group. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-7.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify that the received packet contains the complete VRRP packet (including fixed fields, and IPvX address)." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. TestDecodeV3DiscardsIncompletePacket switched its IPv4 golden to G2 and recomputes in the default form, so the truncation and short-address cases still fail on ErrTruncated or ErrLength and not on ErrChecksum. The earlier residual about the mis-aimed N2 tag stands. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-7.1-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 7.1 says "If any one of the above checks fails, the receiver MUST discard the packet". TestInstanceRxValidAdvertReachesFSM changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same. TestInstanceRxFailedCheckIsDiscarded is unchanged, and an overlay mutant giving instance.lookup the wrong checksum mode reddened both, so the discard path is still exercised end to end. The owner-check carve-out under erratum 8298 stands. Verdict unchanged.

RFC5798-7.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after d2abad70ad). RFC 5798 Section 7.2 says "The following operations MUST be performed when transmitting a VRRP packet: - Fill in the VRRP packet fields with the appropriate virtual router configuration state - Compute the VRRP checksum", and Section 5.2.8 defines that checksum over "the entire VRRP message starting with the version field and a \"pseudo-header\"" for both families. Fill clause: proven. TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState reds when doSendAdvert sends the configured instead of the effective priority, TestSendAdvertFillsFieldsAndChecksum pins every field through encodeLocked, TestEncodeGoldenV3IPv4 pins WriteTo, and the TestBoundaryInterval negative pins Validate refusing an interval the field cannot carry. IPv4 checksum clause (opt-in rfc5798-compatible, since RFC 9568 obsoletes the default form): proven. Overlay mutants run 2026-10-18 over the whole vrrp tree: doSendAdvert hard-coded to ChecksumRFC9568 reds the compatible subtest of TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState (the gap the previous verdict reported is closed); encodeLocked ignoring p.Checksum, or skipping FillChecksum, reds TestSendAdvertFillsFieldsAndChecksum, whose expected sum the test computes itself; G2c 0xDEFB was re-derived independently. IPv6 checksum clause: unproven by any tagged unit. On IPv6 the kernel computes the checksum because openV6 (backend_linux.go) sets IPV6_CHECKSUM 6; the transport unit test uses a fake backend and its IPv6 frame carries no checksum, and the IPv6 run of TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState calls FillChecksum in the test body, not on the production path. Removing that setsockopt leaves every tagged test green (reasoned: only TestIntegrationOpenInstanceSocketOptions and TestIntegrationAdvertV6OnWire, integration-tagged QEMU units, read IPV6_CHECKSUM; the overlay run could not build because another session's internal/component/iface/config_apply.go has undefined applyVLANMTU). Fix: tag TestIntegrationOpenInstanceSocketOptions or TestIntegrationAdvertV6OnWire positive for this row and take its QEMU discrimination record. Summary nit: the {superseded} marker names only RFC9568-7.2-1, but this row also carries the checksum step whose successor is RFC9568-7.2-5. The discrimination records on this row are body-panic replacements and prove reachability only; the deciding logic is proven by the mutants above. No tagged unit is a QEMU-guest unit.

Single-polarity per the row annotation. Verdict unchanged; the guest record is owed a re-record.

RFC5798-7.2-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 7.2 says "Set the IPvX protocol to VRRP - Send the VRRP packet to the VRRP IPvX multicast group". TestTxAdvertV4OnWire and TestSendAdvertV3IPv4HeaderTTLProtoDst changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same; protocol 112 and 224.0.0.18 are still compared with literals. RFC5798-8.1.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 5798 Section 8.1.1 says "If a VRRP router is acting as Master for virtual router(s) containing addresses it does not own, then it must determine which virtual router the packet was sent to when selecting the redirect source address." TestVRRPRedirectSourceFollowsVirtualMAC changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same; the redirect-source capture and its physical-MAC control are unchanged. Verdict unchanged; the guest record is owed a re-record.
